topSignals.title: PJM's proposed 50 MW netting threshold for behind-the-meter generation is still pending at FERC — and had not previously been flagged in this monitor.
topSignals.text: PJM's Feb 23, 2026 compliance filing (responding to FERC's Dec 18, 2025 co-location order) would bar "netting" for new behind-the-meter loads above 50 MW, excluding backup generation from the calculation, with a 3-year transition and grandfathering for existing contracts; three new colocated-load transmission services would apply above that threshold, with rates to follow in a later filing. No FERC ruling on the threshold itself was found in any Oct 2026 source checked today — it remains an open proceeding. SPP's parallel "High Impact Large Load" framework, with a comparable 75 MW threshold, was already approved Jan 14, 2026. So what for INOCEL: this is the first concrete regulatory mechanism found that would strip netting-based cost benefits from new BTM/islanded SOFC installations above 50 MW in PJM territory (NJ, PA, OH, VA, MD, etc.) — exactly the scale of several Bloom/FuelCell Energy data-center deals already tracked in this monitor — while leaving smaller modular SOFC configurations under 50 MW unaffected; worth a dedicated regulatory-risk line in the LCOE model distinguishing PJM BTM deployments above vs. below the threshold. Data Center Frontier | Utility Dive | Mondaq/Davis Graham

Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW, Finland), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative with Hyaxxium, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

PJM's 50 MW behind-the-meter netting threshold (Top Signal #1)* is the day's substantive item — see above for full detail; no FERC ruling found yet. Separately, a state-policy roundup (MultiState, Oct 13) not previously logged in this monitor catalogs the broader US behind-the-meter legislative landscape relevant to islanded/BTM SOFC economics: seven states enacted BTM-enabling laws in 2025 (Oklahoma SB 480, Ohio HB 15, Utah SB 132, Texas SB 6, New Hampshire HB 672, West Virginia HB 2014, New Mexico HB 93), while 2026 activity has shifted toward consumer-protection constraints as opposition has grown — New Jersey's A 796 encourages non-carbon-emitting large-load generation, Maryland's SB 596/HB 940 would require 25% of large-load capacity from backup storage or demand response, and Connecticut's HB 5469 would require customers of 50 MW+ to source 100% of their power from colocated or off-grid generation (favorable, in principle, to a fully islanded SOFC configuration). Germany's Netzpaket/EEG 2027 timeline remains unchanged at a Bundestag second/third reading targeted for the week of Nov 9–13, Bundesrat review Nov 20; the KWK-Gesetz (CHP law) cabinet consideration remains undated past its Oct 14 target. US ITC 45V/48E status and Virginia/Texas/Ireland/EU data-center energy legislation are otherwise unchanged.

lcoe.text: Carry-forward, unchanged:* Virginia data-center electricity tax ($0.011/kWh); PJM Reliability Backstop ceiling (~$202.6/kW-year avoided-cost benchmark, filing suspended pending Feb 28, 2027 paper hearing); FCEL Torrington capex ($200–275M for 350–500 MW/yr by 2028); AEP/Bloom bundled utility-purchase benchmark ($2,944/kW capital+service); Germany's Netzpaket redispatch-curtailment risk (18–20% uncompensated annual-output exposure) for non-islanded SOFC deployments.

Pending calendar (updated):* PJM's 50 MW BTM netting threshold — FERC ruling awaited, no date given, now on this monitor's watch list; German Netzpaket/EEG 2027 Bundestag vote targeted for the week of Nov 9–13 (~2–2.5 weeks out), Bundesrat Nov 20; German KWK-Gesetz cabinet consideration remains undated past its Oct 14 target; FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 10 (16 days out); PJM backstop paper hearing runs to Feb 28, 2027; next EIA STEO Nov 10, 2026 (16 days).
